messages.content:
You answer questions about the GitLab company handbook using ONLY the numbered passages provided.
- Base every statement on the passages and cite them like [1] or [2][3].
- If the passages do not contain the answer, reply exactly: "I don't know based on the handbook." Do not guess or use outside knowledge.
- If the answer depends on a country, entity or situation, say which one the passage covers.
- Be concise: at most 3 sentences.

Passages:
[1] [People Policies - GitLab Inc (USA) > Equal Employment Opportunity Policy > Individuals with Disabilities Policy > Determining Appropriate Accommodations]
When a team member requests a change in the job or working conditions and relates the need to a medical condition, or notifies GitLab "the company" of medical restrictions, the manager or supervisor should direct the team member to open a ticket in Compass or notify the Team Member Relations Team (teammemberrelations@gitlab.com) of the request.  The Team Member Relations Team will then follow the steps outlined below.

Frequently, when a qualified individual with a disability requests a reasonable accommodation, the appropriate accommodation is easily agreed upon. The individual may recommend an accommodation based on their life or work experience. The ultimate decision as to whether a particular accommodation will be made rests with the Company. When the appropriate accommodation is not obvious, the Company may assist the individual in identifying one. If more than one accommodation will enable the individual to perform the job, the Company reserves the right to choose which accommodation it will make. If you feel that you have been unreasonably denied an accommodation request, please speak with the Team Member Relations Team by emailing `teammemberrelations@gitlab.com`. If you have any questions concerning this policy you should speak with the People Operations team.

**Members Requesting Accommodations**

[2] [GitLab India Private Limited EOP Policy > 1.1 Policy Statement > 1.2 Scope > 1.4 Facilities and Amenities > Reasonable Accommodation]
If a team member requires an accommodation to be made for them, a request for accommodation should be made by following [the reasonable accommodation request process set out in the Handbook](/handbook/people-policies/#team-members-requesting-accommodations). Candidates should follow the [candidate accessibility and accommodation request process set out in the Handbook](/handbook/hiring/talent-acquisition-framework/coordinator/#candidate-accessibility-and-accommodation-request-process). Preference may be given to persons with special needs while allotting such accommodation.

[3] [Relocation > Relocation / Address Change > How To Apply for a Long-Term Relocation > Country Specific Tasks > India]
##### Relocating **to or from** India

- The IT Ops team and Accounting team need to be tagged by the People Operations team in the respective [relocation issue](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/people-group/people-operations/employment-templates/-/blob/main/.gitlab/issue_templates/relocations.md) when a team member is relocation to or from India. The IT Ops team will then arrange local laptop procurement and confirm whether the team member is due a refresh. The team member's existing laptop should be disposed of at the originating entity prior to relocation.

[4] [Relocation > Relocation / Address Change > Importance of Communicating Location]
Additionally, certain roles require team members to be present in the location for which they were hired to support business activities.  Sales, for example, may require travel to customer sites and for the team member to be available for customers within a specific time zone.  All Team members are required to obtain manager approval to work outside of their primary location regardless of the length of time at that location. Managers can deny a request or ask for a team member to change their request due to the impact on business results. A team member who fails to communicate and/or seek approval to work outside of their primary location could also result in underperformance management action or loss of employment, depending on the circumstances. Long-term relocations (greater than 183 days/6 months stay) must follow the application and approval process [outlined below](/handbook/people-group/relocation/#how-to-apply-for-a-long-term-relocation).

[5] [Relocation > Relocation / Address Change > How To Apply for a Long-Term Relocation > Approvals Phase > Relocations To New Country or Different Location Factor]
   - If the relocation request within the same country does not result in a change in compensation, no further approvals are required and The People Operations team will [inform the manager of the relocation](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Zq_sxT3ASsnLeTNFJV3-HE5aG3ebv_JXMzhW1zXcEQI/edit)
   - If the country and/or the location factor changes, the compensation will be adjusted based on the location factor change.  For example, if a team member currently resides in a location with a location factor of .70 and the move results in the team member landing in a location with a location factor of .75, the compensation recommendation will be to increase the salary to position the team member's salary to an equal position in the new range (compa-ratio).  If the team member currently resides in a location with a location factor of .80 and the move results in landing in a location with a location factor of .70, the compensation recommendation will be to decrease the salary to position the team member's salary in an equal position in the new range. If the compensation range of the team member's role isn't available, the People Operations Team member reaches out to Total Rewards to discuss the new compensation.
   - If the relocation meets all requirements for a compensation change, the People Operations Team will [determine relocation salary](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1lfWhPWOdQOpbORMiOawcQYpI4QWW8lpKetnWkneEkjE/edit#gid=341502022) using the same compa ratio as the previous location (if applicable).

[6] [GitLab India Private Limited EOP Policy > 1.1 Policy Statement > 1.2 Scope > 1.4 Facilities and Amenities > 1.6 Other Facilities]
_Leave_ - GitLab may, based on a team member's request for leave which exceeds six consecutive days, for a reason related to their disability, administer the leave as a leave of absence through the GitLab Sick Time policy, under which eligible team members will receive 100% paid leave for up to 25 working days. GitLab’s Sick Time policy is administered concurrently with any statutory sick leave for which a team member may be eligible. This will be treated as a request for reasonable accommodation and will be evaluated accordingly. Team members should follow the [process in the Handbook for requesting this leave of absence](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#for-sick-absences-that-exceed-6-consecutive-days).

_Training and Career development_ - GitLab does not discriminate in providing training opportunities and any such opportunities would be available to all team members regardless of their protected characteristics. Every effort will be made to accommodate any special needs of team members by making reasonable adjustments to working arrangements. This applies to all aspects of employment, including training.

Question: In India, if a team member with a disability requests a temporary relocation to a different office location to accommodate their needs, does the Team Member Relations Team have the authority to approve or deny this request, and what criteria would they use to make that decision?
